Issued at 211 AM EDT Fri Oct 2 2026

As CAA dwindles early this morning over the Upper Great Lakes, 
expect to see some lake effect cloud cover develop over portions of 
the northwest wind belts, particularly over the eastern U.P. where 
there is a longer fetch upstream over Lake Superior. While delta-Ts 
look to be in the lower teens, it should be enough to kick-start 
some light rain/drizzle lake effect showers over the eastern U.P. 
this morning into potentially early this afternoon, especially since 
gusty northwest winds could kick up to around 30 mph along the 
lakeshore from the Keweenaw to Whitefish Point. However, with 
shortwave high pressure ridging already beginning to move into the 
area today, expect the lake effect rain/drizzle showers and the 
breezy conditions to weaken with time, with the showers ending by 
the late afternoon hours over the east. While we may see some 
remnant lake effect cloud cover hanging on over the eastern U.P. 
early this evening, expect mostly clear skies by tonight as the 
center of the sfc ridging moves overhead. With the skies being clear 
and the antecedent air being quite cool, expect temperatures in the 
areas away from the Great Lakes to drop below freezing, with the 
typical cold spots in the interior west potentially dropping down to 
as low as the lower 20s late tonight/early Saturday morning. 
Therefore, a Freeze Warning has been issued for western and central 
Upper MI from 10 PM EDT tonight to 10 AM EDT Saturday. In addition, 
given that the ridging will create nearly calm winds at the sfc, 
widespread frost is expected across the U.P. save the areas north of 
Houghton. 

Outside of the light lake effect rain showers and Freeze Warning 
headlines for tonight, overall expect cooler and more seasonable 
temperatures this weekend into early next week as a Clipper low 
approaches and eventually passes the area. This means that high 
temperatures are projected to range from the mid-50s to mid-60s 
across the U.P. today through next Monday, while lows drop into the 
20s and 30s in the interior areas tonight through Monday night (save 
for Saturday night when clouds and rainfall from the Clipper moving 
through limit lows to the 40s). 

Speaking of the Clipper, while cloud cover from it looks to move 
into the west as early as early Saturday morning, dry air in the 
lower levels looks to prevent anything from reach the ground until 
late in the day. However, as the center of the Clipper 'clips' (*buh 
dum tiss*) northern Lake Superior Saturday night, CAMs and medium 
range guidance suggest some light rainfall passing over us during 
the overnight hours. While nearly all guidance suggests the highest 
rainfall amounts north of the U.P. Saturday night into Sunday 
morning, the latest REFS run has a general 50 to 100% chance of at 
least a tenth of an inch of rain falling over the area Saturday 
night, with the exception being a less than 50% chance south of US-2 
in Menominee County. While some lake effect sprinkles could be seen 
behind the Clipper during the day Sunday over the northwest wind 
belts, incoming ridging will put an end to it by the end of the day. 
In addition to the rain chances, height falls up to 4 mb/3 hrs and 
height rises up to 3 mb/3 hrs ahead of and behind the Clipper, 
respectively, indicate breezy southerly winds preceding the 
Clipper's arrival on Saturday followed by gusty northwest winds 
behind it on Sunday; some northwesterly wind gusts up to 40 mph will 
be possible over the Keweenaw and along the Lake Superior shoreline 
from Marquette County eastward. While the latest NBM shows a 50 to 
70% chance for northwest wind gusts over 40 mph for these areas on 
Sunday, I believe the NBM is running too hot on the wind gusts and 
the actual chances will be somewhere between 20 and 60% like what is 
shown in the latest LREF run. 

Moving into next week, expect shortwave ridging to keep the area dry 
on Monday while another Clipper brings troughing back to the area 
next Tuesday. However, expect the Clipper's passing to be dry, which 
could increase fire weather concerns ahead of and behind the 
Clipper's passage next week. Moving towards the end of next week, 
medium range guidance slightly differs on the strength of the jet 
stream progging along the U.S./Canada border. Should the jet stream 
be stronger, we could see some light rain chances return as well as 
more 'normal Fall-like' temperatures continuing; if not, then we 
could see a warm-up again to high temperatures returning to the 60s 
across most of the area.
